name: Bishkek Soviet Heritage City Tour - Day Trip
summary: A private half-day around Bishkek with one of our English-speaking guides. You start among the stalls of Osh Bazaar, then move on to Ala-Too Square, the National History Museum, Victory Square and the Central Mosque. On the way we talk about Soviet times, the revolutions and life in the city today. A good first day in Kyrgyzstan, at a pace set by your interests.
highlights: Spices, dried fruit and crafts at Osh Bazaar
Changing of the guard by the Manas Monument
Stone Age to modern Kyrgyz at the History Museum
Soviet marble halls, Victory Square, Central Mosque

blurb.hook: Soviet squares, a busy bazaar and the story of modern Kyrgyzstan.
blurb.text: A private half-day with a local guide: Osh Bazaar, Ala-Too Square, the History Museum and the Soviet landmarks that shaped the capital.

itinerary.title: Osh Bazaar to the Central Mosque
desc: Your guide collects you from your hotel and the day opens at Osh Bazaar. Stalls of spices, dried fruit, fresh produce and handicrafts fill the lanes. Your guide helps you find local products and explains the habits behind them. Note that the bazaar is closed on Mondays.

Next is the Philharmonic Hall, built of white marble and lit by stained glass. We pass the Mayor's Office, then drive by the White House, the seat of government. Here you hear about the revolutions of 2005, 2010 and 2020 and how the country is run today.

On Ala-Too Square you stand below the 33-metre Manas Monument and the 100-metre flagpole. We try to time the stop for the changing of the Guard of Honor. Nearby, the National History Museum follows the region from the Stone Age and Iron Age to Kyrgyz culture and identity. The museum also closes on Mondays.

The Opera and Ballet Theatre, Victory Square with its Eternal Flame and the Ottoman-style Central Mosque round off the route. At Victory Square your guide explains what the Second World War meant for families here. Before the drop-off we can stop at Navat, Faiza or Mubarak for a meal you pay for yourself.
itinerary.transfer: Hotel pick-up and drop-off in Bishkek

name: Bishkek 3-Stop Food Tasting Tour - Day Trip
summary: Four hours of Bishkek through its food. With a private English-speaking guide you visit Osh Bazaar, three local food spots and the main sights in between. Expect kattama with samovar tea, a full table of lagman, plov, manty and samsa at Faiza, and dessert with green tea to finish. Made for travellers who like to learn a city by eating.
highlights: Kattama flatbread with tea from a samovar
Lagman, plov, manty and samsa at Faiza
Tasting snacks and bargaining at Osh Bazaar
Ala-Too Square and the Manas Monument between meals

blurb.hook: Three stops, one bazaar and the dishes locals actually eat.
blurb.text: A private four-hour food tour: kattama and samovar tea, a big lunch at Faiza, dessert with green tea, and the main Bishkek sights between tastings.

itinerary.title: Osh Bazaar, three tastings and the city centre
desc: We pick you up at your hotel and head straight to Osh Bazaar, the liveliest market in town. You wander past spices, fresh produce and snacks, try a few bites and chat with the vendors. Your guide shows you how to bargain the local way, and there is time for souvenirs.

The first tasting is at a small café. You get kattama, a crisp Kyrgyz flatbread, with tea boiled in a samovar. Then we walk the centre: Ala-Too Square for the changing of the guard, the Manas Monument, the White House, the Lenin Monument and Panfilov Park. The Philharmonic Hall and the Opera and Ballet Theatre show the city's cultural side.

The main meal is at Faiza, a restaurant locals love. Plates of lagman, plov, manty and samsa keep coming, and you eat as much as you like. Afterwards a short drive takes you to Victory Square and past the Central Mosque.
The last stop is a stylish restaurant for a traditional dessert and green tea. It is a quiet moment to talk over the day. Then your guide drives you back to your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Hotel pick-up and drop-off in Bishkek
itinerary.meals: Tastings at 3 stops, main meal at Faiza

name: Dinner & Boorsok in a Kyrgyz Home - Day Trip
summary: An evening with a Kyrgyz family in their Bishkek home. Our driver brings you to the house, where elders, parents and children welcome you. You help in the kitchen with boorsok, then sit down to a dinner cooked by the mother of the house. One family member speaks English, so questions about traditions and daily life come easily.
highlights: A dinner cooked by the mother of the house
Frying boorsok with the family in their kitchen
Talk with elders, parents and kids over the meal
A family photo together before you leave

blurb.hook: Not a restaurant. A real family table in Bishkek.
blurb.text: Spend an evening in a local home: help fry boorsok, share a homemade Kyrgyz dinner and ask the family anything. One of them speaks English.

itinerary.title: An evening with a Bishkek family
desc: Our driver collects you from your hotel and brings you to the family's house in Bishkek. Elders, parents, teenagers and children are all there to greet you. The mood is easy from the first minute.

Soon you are invited into the kitchen. You help make boorsok, small pieces of fried bread, and watch an everyday meal come together. The mother of the house cooks the rest from the recipes she uses daily.

At the table you share several homemade Kyrgyz dishes. Talk turns to customs, family values and ordinary life, with plenty of time for your questions. One family member speaks English, so nothing gets lost.
You can look around the home and see how it is arranged. Photos are welcome, and you can take a family picture together. After dinner you say goodbye, and the driver takes you back to your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Hotel pick-up and drop-off in Bishkek

name: Ala-Archa Gorge Hike at Your Pace - Day Trip
summary: A day in Ala-Archa National Park, about 40 km and an hour's drive from Bishkek. Your guide checks your fitness and picks the route: an easy river walk, a hike to a viewpoint or the harder trail toward Ak-Sai Waterfall. Squirrels and birds eat from your hand, and lunch is included. It suits families, couples and solo travellers.
highlights: Easy river walk or the trail toward Ak-Sai Waterfall
Squirrels and birds that eat from your hand
Optional cable car up to wide Tien Shan views
Lunch in the park or at a local spot in Bishkek

blurb.hook: Snowy Tien Shan peaks one hour from Bishkek, at the pace you choose.
blurb.text: A guided day in Ala-Archa Gorge: river walks, viewpoints or a push toward Ak-Sai Waterfall, hand-fed squirrels and a Kyrgyz lunch included.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ala-Archa Gorge and back
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel and we drive about 40 km into the mountains. The ride takes around an hour. The city falls behind fast, and the air turns cool and alpine.

Ala-Archa Gorge opens up with its river, pine forest, alpine meadows and snowy peaks above. Your guide asks how fit you feel and what you enjoy, then suggests a route. The pace changes whenever you need it to.

For an easy day, walk along the river and the valley floor, which works well for families. The optional cable car gives you mountain views with no effort. Feeling strong? Hike to a viewpoint or keep going toward Ak-Sai Waterfall, the hardest option of the day, with your guide beside you the whole way.
Lunch is your choice. Eat at a restaurant inside the park, or drive back to Bishkek for a place where locals eat and the Kyrgyz menu is longer. Afterwards we drop you at your hotel.

name: Bishkek & Ala-Archa in One Day - Day Trip
summary: Mountains first, the capital after lunch. We drive about an hour to Ala-Archa National Park for a walk or hike that fits your level, then eat a Kyrgyz lunch and head into Bishkek. Osh Bazaar, Ala-Too Square, Soviet landmarks and the Central Mosque fill the second half. Ideal if you have one free day and want both sides of the country.
highlights: Shuttle bus ride deep into Ala-Archa Gorge
River walk, viewpoint hike or Ak-Sai Waterfall
A bargaining lesson at Osh Bazaar
Soviet Bishkek, from the Circus to the Wedding Hall

blurb.hook: One day, two sides of Kyrgyzstan: Ala-Archa and Bishkek.
blurb.text: Walk or hike in Ala-Archa Gorge, sit down to a Kyrgyz lunch, then explore Osh Bazaar, Ala-Too Square and Soviet Bishkek with your guide.

itinerary.title: Ala-Archa Gorge, then Bishkek city
desc: Your guide picks you up at your hotel and asks what matters most to you: nature, culture or an even mix. The plan bends around that answer. Then we drive about an hour to Ala-Archa National Park, talking about local life on the way.

At the park we leave the car and ride a local shuttle bus deeper into the gorge. From there you choose a calm river walk, a moderate hike to a viewpoint or the longer push toward Ak-Sai Waterfall. The optional cable car lifts you to wide views without the climb.

Lunch is at a restaurant in the park or at a local place back in Bishkek with a bigger choice of Kyrgyz dishes. Your guide suggests what fits your day. The city part then starts at Osh Bazaar, with local products, souvenirs and a lesson in bargaining.

On Ala-Too Square you see the 33-metre Manas Monument, the 100-metre flagpole and, with good timing, the changing of the Guard of Honor. At the White House your guide tells the story of the 2005, 2010 and 2020 revolutions, then the route runs past the Lenin Monument, through Panfilov Park and on to Victory Square. The Philharmonic Hall, Opera and Ballet Theatre, Circus and Wedding Hall each show a different period of Soviet design. We finish at the Central Mosque, talk about faith in Kyrgyzstan today, and drive you back to your hotel.
itinerary.meals: Lunch at a traditional Kyrgyz restaurant

name: Ala-Archa & Chunkurchak Gorges - Day Trip
summary: Two mountain gorges near Bishkek in a single day. In Ala-Archa National Park you walk, hike or ride the cable car while squirrels and birds eat from your hand. In Chunkurchak Gorge you cross the Sky Bridge, see Pigeon Waterfall and can add horse riding, archery or a zipline. Your guide shapes the plan for families, couples and active travellers.
highlights: Walk across the Sky Bridge in Chunkurchak Gorge
Pigeon Waterfall and wide alpine meadows
Hand-feeding squirrels and birds in Ala-Archa
Optional horse riding, archery or zipline

blurb.hook: Two gorges in one day: forest trails, then the Sky Bridge.
blurb.text: River walks and hand-fed squirrels in Ala-Archa, then Chunkurchak for the Sky Bridge, Pigeon Waterfall and optional horse rides or a zipline.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ala-Archa and Chunkurchak and back
desc: We collect you at your hotel and ask how you want the day to feel: more nature, more activities or a mix. The plan follows your answer. It is about an hour to Ala-Archa, and your guide talks about the Tien Shan and local life as the city fades.

We leave the car and take a local shuttle bus deeper into Ala-Archa Gorge. Choose an easy river walk, a moderate hike to a viewpoint or the tougher trail toward Ak-Sai Waterfall. The optional cable car gives you the views without the effort, and birds and squirrels may come to eat from your hand.

Next we drive on to Chunkurchak Gorge, where the land opens into alpine meadows and wide valleys. You walk across the Sky Bridge and visit Pigeon Waterfall, with time for photos at your own pace. Horse riding, archery or a zipline are there if you want more action.

We also stop at Supara Chunkurchak, one of the best-known ethno-complexes in Kyrgyzstan. You can rest here and have lunch with a mountain view, paid on the spot. At the end of the day we drive you back to your hotel in Bishkek.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Ala-Archa · 1 h, then on to Chunkurchak
itinerary.meals: Lunch at Supara, at your own cost

name: Silk Road Burana Tower & Bishkek - Day Trip
summary: A history day that links the Silk Road to modern Bishkek. We drive about 80 km into the Chui Valley to Burana Tower, the ruins of Balasagun, the balbal stones and the petroglyphs. After a Kyrgyz lunch on the way back, the rest of the day belongs to Osh Bazaar, Ala-Too Square and the city's Soviet architecture. Good for travellers who like the stories behind old stones.
highlights: Climb Burana Tower for views over the Chui Valley
Balbal stone figures and petroglyphs at Balasagun
Old coins and ceramics in the site museum
Changing of the guard on Ala-Too Square

blurb.hook: From a Silk Road tower to Soviet Bishkek in one day.
blurb.text: Explore Burana Tower and the ruins of Balasagun in the Chui Valley, stop for a Kyrgyz lunch, then tour Osh Bazaar and Ala-Too Square with your guide.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Burana Tower and back, with a city tour
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel and asks whether you lean toward history, culture or a balance of both. Then we drive about 80 km into the Chui Valley. On the way you hear why the Silk Road mattered so much here.

At Burana you walk among the remains of Balasagun, once a busy trading town. Balbals, the old carved stone figures, stand near ancient petroglyphs. A small museum on site keeps coins, ceramics and other finds from the area. Climb the tower itself for a wide view across the valley.

Lunch is at a local restaurant on the road back to Bishkek. The city tour starts at Osh Bazaar, where you can taste local products, buy souvenirs and practise bargaining. On Ala-Too Square you see the 33-metre Manas Monument and the 100-metre flagpole, and with good timing the changing of the Guard of Honor.

Your guide covers the 2005, 2010 and 2020 revolutions at the White House, then leads you past the Lenin Monument, through Panfilov Park and to Victory Square. The Philharmonic Hall, Opera and Ballet Theatre, Circus and Wedding Hall show several eras of Soviet building. The last stop is the Central Mosque, before the drive back to your hotel.

name: Konorchek Canyon Hike & Burana - Day Trip
summary: We start at Burana Tower, the last standing piece of the Silk Road town of Balasagun, with its balbals, petroglyphs and a small museum. Then the scenery turns red. We hike into Konorchek Canyon, past wind-cut cliffs, to the viewpoint over the Eolian Castles. An easy to moderate walk for travellers who want history and a proper leg stretch in one day.
highlights: Climb Burana Tower for views over the Tien Shan
Balbals, petroglyphs and a museum of Balasagun finds
A 2-3 hour canyon hike to the Eolian Castles viewpoint
Kattama bread and samovar tea before the trail

blurb.hook: Silk Road ruins in the morning, red canyon walls by midday.
blurb.text: Burana Tower and its museum, then an easy to moderate hike through Konorchek Canyon to the Eolian Castles. Kyrgyz lunch at a local cafe on the way home.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Burana Tower and Konorchek Canyon
desc: Your guide picks you up at your hotel in Bishkek. Tell us whether you lean towards history or nature, and we shape the day around it. Burana Tower is about 80 km away, and the Silk Road stories start in the car.

Burana stands on the site of Balasagun, once a busy trading town. You walk among balbals and petroglyphs, then look at coins, ceramics and other finds from the 9th to 11th centuries in the small museum. Climb the tower if you like. The Tien Shan fills the horizon from the top.

Next comes Konorchek Canyon, and the landscape changes completely. First we stop at a small local place for kattama and tea from a samovar. Then we walk up the valley for 2 to 3 hours there and back. The trail is easy to moderate, with a few spots that need care, and red cliffs rise on both sides.

The path ends at the Eolian Castles, a wide viewpoint where we rest and take photos. Your guide stays with you the whole way and sets the pace. On the drive back to Bishkek we stop for lunch at a local cafe, then drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Burana Tower · 80 km, then on to Konorchek Canyon
itinerary.meals: Kattama and samovar tea, Kyrgyz lunch at a local cafe

name: Kol-Tor Lake Hike & Burana Tower - Day Trip
summary: A day for people who like to earn their view. We visit Burana Tower first, where the Silk Road town of Balasagun once stood. Then we drive into the mountains and hike 4 to 5 hours there and back to Kol-Tor Lake at 2,725 m, through pine forest and across small streams. Moderate, sometimes steep, and well within reach with basic fitness.
highlights: Turquoise water of Kol-Tor Lake at 2,725 m
Pine forest, small river crossings and open slopes
Lunch box by the lake, trekking poles provided
Burana Tower and its petroglyphs before the trail

blurb.hook: A Silk Road tower, then a turquoise lake at 2,725 m.
blurb.text: Morning at Burana Tower, then a moderate 4 to 5 hour hike through pine forest to Kol-Tor Lake. Lunch box by the water, poles provided, a horse on request.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Burana Tower and Kol-Tor Lake
desc: We pick you up from your hotel in Bishkek early in the morning. Tell your guide how you feel about hiking, and we set the pace from there. Burana Tower is about 80 km away, a comfortable drive with plenty of local stories.

At Burana you walk the grounds of Balasagun, a Silk Road trading town. Petroglyphs and finds from the 9th to 11th centuries show how people lived here. You can climb the tower for a wide view of the valley and the Tien Shan. It is a calm start before the mountains.

Then we drive to the Kol-Tor trailhead. The hike takes 4 to 5 hours there and back and is moderate, with some steady climbs. You start in pine forest, cross small rivers and come out onto open slopes. Trekking poles are included, and you can ride a horse up instead if you ask in advance.

Kol-Tor Lake sits at 2,725 m, turquoise from glacial minerals and ringed by peaks. We rest here with a lunch box of sandwiches, fruit and snacks. Then we walk down to the car and drive back to your hotel in Bishkek.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Burana Tower · 80 km, then on to Kol-Tor

name: First Horse Ride in Ala-Archa - Day Trip
summary: Ala-Archa is about 40 minutes from Bishkek, which makes it the easiest place to try riding in the mountains. A local horseman and calm, well-trained horses take you on a 2-hour ride along the slopes above the valley. Afterwards we walk by the river deeper in the park. Made for beginners and anyone who wants a gentle first time in the saddle.
highlights: A 2-hour ride on calm horses, beginners welcome
Slope-top views the footpaths don't reach
Riverside forest walk with squirrels and birds
Optional cable car up to a high viewpoint

blurb.hook: Your first ride in the mountains, 40 minutes from Bishkek.
blurb.text: A 2-hour beginner-friendly ride with a local horseman in Ala-Archa National Park, then a gentle riverside walk and lunch your way.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ala-Archa National Park and back
desc: Your guide collects you from your hotel in Bishkek. The drive to Ala-Archa National Park takes about 40 minutes, and the city gives way to forest and peaks quickly.

At the start you meet your horseman and your horse. A short safety briefing covers the basics. Then you ride for 2 hours along the mountain slopes, with views across the valley, the river and the Tien Shan. The pace stays easy, and your guide and horseman stay close the whole time.

After the ride, a shuttle bus takes us deeper into the park. We walk along the river through the forest at whatever pace suits you. Squirrels and birds come close here, and a walk further uphill can bring more wildlife and wider views. If your legs are done, the cable car lifts you to a high viewpoint with no effort.
Lunch is your choice. Eat at one of the restaurants inside the park, or bring a picnic and eat by the river. Your guide helps you pick. Then we drive back and drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.meals: Lunch at your own cost, in the park or as a picnic

name: Chunkurchak Sky Bridge & Archery - Day Trip
summary: Chunkurchak Gorge is one of the closest mountain escapes from Bishkek. We cross the Sky Bridge, walk down to Pigeon Waterfall, then spend the rest of the day at a mountain retreat. Ride a horse through the forest, try a Kyrgyz archery masterclass, take the zipline or simply sit by the river. You choose on the spot and pay only for what you do.
highlights: Walk across the Sky Bridge above the gorge
Get close to the water at Pigeon Waterfall
Kyrgyz archery masterclass or a forest horse ride
Lunch at the Supara ethno-complex or a picnic

blurb.hook: A sky bridge, a waterfall and a bow in your hands.
blurb.text: Sky Bridge and Pigeon Waterfall in Chunkurchak Gorge, then horse riding, archery or a zipline as you like. A slow, flexible day close to Bishkek.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chunkurchak Gorge and back
desc: Your guide picks you up at your hotel in Bishkek. It is a short, scenic drive to Chunkurchak Gorge, and the river and mountain air take over fast.
First stop is the Sky Bridge. You walk across it with the whole gorge open below. Then we head to Pigeon Waterfall, where a path leads down to the water.

The rest of the day is yours to plan. Ride through forest and along river trails, join a Kyrgyz archery masterclass, try the zipline or the cable car, or just walk and rest by the river. Everything is booked on the spot, so you pay only for what you choose. Your guide suggests the best local options.

For lunch, eat a Kyrgyz meal at the Supara ethno-resort or bring a picnic. If you want a prepared picnic or to cook outdoors, tell us ahead and we help with the gear. We drive back when you are ready, usually late in the afternoon, and drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Chunkurchak Gorge and back
itinerary.meals: Lunch at your own cost, at Supara or as a picnic

name: Chong-Kemin National Park Ride - Day Trip
summary: A riding day with a Silk Road start. We visit Burana Tower, stop in Boom Gorge for kattama and samovar tea, then head into Chong-Kemin National Park. There you ride 3 to 4 hours through forest, along rivers and over open meadows. The day ends at a Kyrgyz family's table with a homemade meal. Good for first-timers and experienced riders alike.
highlights: A 3-4 hour ride through forest, rivers and meadows
Riding lesson first, route matched to your level
Homemade lunch in a Kyrgyz family home
Burana Tower and samovar tea on the way

blurb.hook: Ride the forests and meadows of Chong-Kemin, then eat with a local family.
blurb.text: Burana Tower, a tea stop in Boom Gorge, then a 3 to 4 hour ride in Chong-Kemin National Park and a homemade meal with a Kyrgyz family.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Burana Tower
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel in Bishkek and drives you to Burana Tower. This is where Balasagun stood, a Silk Road town of the 9th to 11th centuries. You see petroglyphs and balbals, and a small museum of coins, ceramics and jewellery. Climb the tower for a view of the Tien Shan.
On the road through Boom Gorge we stop at a small place locals love and few visitors find. You try kattama with tea brewed in a samovar.

In Chong-Kemin National Park you meet your horseman and horse. First comes a short lesson on how to sit, steer, stop and stay safe. Your guide picks a calm trail or a livelier one based on your experience. Then you ride for 3 to 4 hours through forest, across rivers and over open slopes, passing small villages.
After the ride, a Kyrgyz family welcomes you into their home for a homemade meal. It is a slow, warm end to the day. Then we drive back to Bishkek and drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Burana Tower and Chong-Kemin, and back
itinerary.meals: Kattama and samovar tea, homemade family lunch

name: Issyk-Kul Shore & Hot Springs - Day Trip
summary: The north shore of Issyk-Kul in one long day from Bishkek. We stop at Burana Tower, drive through Boom Gorge with a kattama and samovar tea break, then explore the open-air petroglyphs and the Ruh Ordo complex. Lunch by the lake, a boat ride from May to September and a soak in the hot springs near Cholpon-Ata before the drive home.
highlights: Open-air petroglyphs and the Ruh Ordo cultural complex
Boat ride and a swim from the deck, May to September
Warm mineral hot springs near Cholpon-Ata
Burana Tower and a samovar tea stop in Boom Gorge

blurb.hook: Burana, Boom Gorge and the north shore of Issyk-Kul, back by night.
blurb.text: Burana Tower, kattama in Boom Gorge, then petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, a lakeside lunch and hot springs near Cholpon-Ata. A long, full day at the lake.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to the north shore of Issyk-Kul and back
desc: Your guide picks you up at your hotel in Bishkek, and we head east towards Issyk-Kul. First stop is Burana Tower, on the site of the Silk Road town of Balasagun. You see petroglyphs, balbals and a small museum of 9th to 11th century coins, ceramics and jewellery. Climb the tower for a wide view of the Tien Shan.
The road then follows the river through Boom Gorge, between high rock walls. We pull over at a small place locals know well for kattama with sour cream and tea boiled in a samovar.

On the north shore we walk through the open-air petroglyphs, rock carvings left by early peoples. Then we visit Ruh Ordo, a quiet complex dedicated to different cultures and faiths. Lunch is at a local restaurant by the lake. From May to September you can take a boat out and, in warm weather, jump in from the deck with a life vest on.

Before heading home, you can relax in the mineral hot springs near Cholpon-Ata, with massages on offer if you want one. Then we drive back through the mountains and reach your hotel in Bishkek late in the evening.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Cholpon-Ata via Boom Gorge, and back
itinerary.activity: Sightseeing · Boat ride and hot springs
itinerary.meals: Kattama and samovar tea, lunch at a lakeside restaurant

name: Burana, Konorchek & Issyk-Kul - Day Trip
summary: Three big sights east of Bishkek in a single day. We start at Burana Tower, take a samovar tea break in Boom Gorge, then hike 2.5 to 3 hours through the red walls of Konorchek Canyon to the Eolian Castles. We finish on the western shore of Issyk-Kul near Balykchy with a Kyrgyz lunch and free time on the beach. A full day for travellers short on time.
highlights: Burana Tower and its 9th to 11th century finds
A 2.5-3 hour hike to the Eolian Castles viewpoint
Kattama with sour cream and samovar tea in Boom Gorge
Lunch and beach time on Issyk-Kul near Balykchy

blurb.hook: Three sights in one day: a tower, a red canyon and Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: Burana Tower, a 2.5 to 3 hour hike in Konorchek Canyon, then lunch and beach time on Issyk-Kul near Balykchy. History, hiking and the lake in one go.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Issyk-Kul via Burana and Konorchek
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel in Bishkek and we set off towards Issyk-Kul. First stop is Burana Tower, where the Silk Road town of Balasagun once stood. You see petroglyphs, balbals and a small museum of 9th to 11th century coins and ceramics. Climb the tower for a view over the valley and the Tien Shan.
The road enters Boom Gorge and runs beside the river between tall rock walls. We stop at a small spot locals know for kattama with sour cream and tea boiled in a samovar.

Then we hike Konorchek Canyon, 2.5 to 3 hours there and back. You walk up a dry riverbed between red cliffs shaped over millions of years. People compare it to the Grand Canyon, some say Mars. The trail ends at a viewpoint over the Eolian Castles, a good place to rest and take photos.

We reach Issyk-Kul, the world's second-largest alpine lake, on its western shore near Balykchy. Lunch is Kyrgyz food at a local restaurant. Afterwards the beach is yours for a walk or a quiet sit. In the evening we drive back and drop you at your hotel in Bishkek.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Balykchy via Boom Gorge, and back
itinerary.meals: Kattama and samovar tea, Kyrgyz lunch by the lake

name: Ak-Say Canyons & Barskoon Falls - Day Trip
summary: A full day on the quieter south shore of Issyk-Kul. We walk the red Ak-Say Canyons, where the lake and the snowy ridges share one view. Then we hike through forest to the Barskoon waterfalls at a pace you choose. Lunch is in a yurt by the shore or by the river. It suits travellers who want more than the busy north shore.
highlights: Red rock viewpoints in the Ak-Say Canyons
Forest trail to the Barskoon waterfalls
Lunch in a yurt by the lake or by the river
Samovar tea and kattama at a local stop

blurb.hook: Red canyons and a waterfall hike on the south shore of Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: One long day from Bishkek: the Ak-Say Canyons, the Barskoon waterfalls and lunch by the lake, with a local guide the whole way.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ak-Say and Barskoon and back
desc: We pick you up from your hotel in Bishkek early in the morning. The road runs through valleys and mountains to the south shore of Issyk-Kul. On the way we stop at a small local place for kattama with sour cream and tea from a samovar. A simple breakfast is possible too.

First comes the Ak-Say Canyons, a maze of red rock that few visitors reach. People often compare it to Mars. From the viewpoints you see the red canyon, the blue lake and the snowy peaks together. There is time for short walks and photos.

Lunch is your call: a yurt on the shore of Issyk-Kul or a picnic by the river. Then we head into Barskoon Gorge. The walk can be an easy 30 minutes or a longer forest hike, and your guide sets the pace with you. At the end you reach the waterfalls, cold air and water falling between cliffs and trees.
If you like, we can add an eagle hunting demonstration in Bokonbayevo in the evening as a paid extra. Then we drive back to Bishkek and drop you at your hotel late in the evening, around 10 to 11 pm.

name: Arashan Gorge Ride & Sky Bridge - Day Trip
summary: A half-day ride in Arashan Gorge, 40 minutes to an hour from Bishkek. You spend two hours in the saddle on mountain paths and open valleys with Tien Shan views. Then you walk across the Sky Bridge above the Pigeon Waterfall. No riding experience needed, and you pick morning or afternoon. Good for a first or last day in Bishkek.
highlights: Two hours on horseback with Tien Shan views
Horse matched to your level, first-timers welcome
Walk the Sky Bridge above the Pigeon Waterfall
Morning or afternoon, back in Bishkek the same day

blurb.hook: Mountains, a horse and a sky bridge, all in half a day.
blurb.text: A two-hour ride in Arashan Gorge close to Bishkek, then the Sky Bridge over the Pigeon Waterfall. Beginners welcome, morning or afternoon.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Arashan Gorge and back
desc: We collect you at your hotel in Bishkek. Tell your guide how much you have ridden before, so we can plan the ride around you. The drive to Arashan Gorge takes 40 minutes to an hour, and the city gives way to mountains fast.

At the gorge you meet the local horseman and your horse, picked for your level. Calm and slow, or a little livelier, it is your choice. You get a short safety talk and simple riding tips before you set off, even if you have never ridden.
The ride lasts two hours on mountain paths and through open valleys, with wide views of the Tien Shan. Your guide and the horseman stay close the whole time and adjust the pace for you.

After the ride we walk across the Sky Bridge above the Pigeon Waterfall. You hear the water below, and the far side opens onto the valley and the cliffs. There is no rush here. Then we drive back and drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.transfer: Bishkek to Arashan Gorge · 40 min to 1 h

name: Winter Ala-Archa Snow Walk - Day Trip
summary: A gentle winter day in Ala-Archa National Park, 40 km from Bishkek. An eco bus takes us deep into the snowy gorge, then you walk at your own pace past frozen river bends and pines under snow. Feed the birds and squirrels, try the short hike to the Broken Heart viewpoint and warm up with a hot drink at the A-Frame. No hard hiking and no long drive.
highlights: Snowy pines and a frozen river, 40 km from Bishkek
Feed the birds and squirrels along the trail
Optional short hike to the Broken Heart viewpoint
Hot drink with a mountain view at the A-Frame

blurb.hook: Ala-Archa under snow, one hour from the city.
blurb.text: An easy winter walk in Ala-Archa National Park with an eco bus ride, birds and squirrels to feed and hot tea at the A-Frame.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ala-Archa and back
desc: Your guide and driver pick you up at your hotel in the morning. Ala-Archa National Park is 40 km away, about an hour by car. On the way in, your guide tells you about the park.

Cars stop at the park entrance. From there the official eco bus, the only transport allowed inside, takes us deeper into the gorge. Out of the bus, you walk the winter road as far as you like. Stop for photos of the icy river, feed the birds and squirrels and keep an eye out for winter wildlife.
Want a little more? Take the short hike to the Broken Heart viewpoint. Your guide stays with you, shows the best spots and helps with photos.

We finish at the A-Frame restaurant with hot tea or coffee and the mountains framed in its big windows. Then the eco bus takes us back to the car and we drive to Bishkek. The whole trip takes 5 to 6 hours.
itinerary.activity: Winter walk · at your own pace

name: Chunkurchak Snow & Hot Springs - Day Trip
summary: A winter day in Chunkurchak Gorge, about an hour from Bishkek. We see the frozen Pigeon Waterfall and the Sky Bridge, then spend the middle of the day at the Chunkurchak ski resort. Ski or snowboard on gentle beginner slopes, ride the cable car, go tubing or take a short ride in the snowy forest. We end the day in a natural hot spring. Fun for all ages.
highlights: Frozen Pigeon Waterfall and the Sky Bridge
Beginner ski slopes, cable car and tubing
Short horse ride through the snowy forest
Warm mineral hot spring with snow all around

blurb.hook: Snow, ice and a hot spring, one hour from Bishkek.
blurb.text: A winter day in Chunkurchak: the frozen Pigeon Waterfall, the Sky Bridge, skiing or tubing at the resort and a soak in a hot spring.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chunkurchak and back
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel and goes over the plan as we drive out of Bishkek toward the mountains. If you want to ski or snowboard, we stop at a rental shop on the way and your guide helps you pick the right gear.

The first stop is the frozen Pigeon Waterfall, a wall of blue ice among snowy cliffs. A short walk away is the Sky Bridge, strung between two cliffs above the white valley. Your guide shows the best viewpoints and helps with photos.

Next is the Chunkurchak ski resort, known for gentle slopes where beginners feel at home. Your guide sorts out lift passes, gear and an instructor if you want a lesson. Ski, snowboard, ride the cable car, go tubing or try the balloon sleds. Prefer it quiet? Take a short horse ride through the snowy forest or warm up in a café. We break for a hot lunch at the resort.
On the way back we stop at a natural hot spring. You sit in warm mineral water with snow all around. Dinner here is possible if you like. Then we drive back to Bishkek and drop you at your hotel.

name: Winter Ala-Archa & Chunkurchak - Day Trip
summary: Two snowy gorges near Bishkek in one day. In Ala-Archa National Park you take the eco bus in, then choose an easy river walk with birds and squirrels or a hike to the Broken Heart viewpoint. In Chunkurchak we see the frozen Pigeon Waterfall, cross the Sky Bridge and ride the chair lift. Gentle walking, good for families and couples.
highlights: Ala-Archa river walk or Broken Heart viewpoint
Frozen Pigeon Waterfall and the Sky Bridge
Chair lift ride over the white Chunkurchak valley
Optional ride in the snowy forest or hot spring

blurb.hook: Ala-Archa and Chunkurchak in snow, back in Bishkek by evening.
blurb.text: A full winter day: an eco bus ride and a walk in Ala-Archa, then the frozen waterfall, the Sky Bridge and a chair lift in Chunkurchak.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Ala-Archa, Chunkurchak and back
desc: We meet you in your hotel lobby and drive toward the mountains. Ala-Archa National Park is less than an hour away. Private cars cannot go inside, so we switch to the eco bus that runs deeper into the valley.
Then you pick your walk. The easy one follows the frozen river, with birds and squirrels to feed. The other climbs to the Broken Heart viewpoint for a wide look at the snowy peaks.

From Ala-Archa we drive on through snowy forest to Chunkurchak Gorge. Your guide walks you down to the frozen Pigeon Waterfall, then across the Sky Bridge between two cliffs. A chair lift takes us to the top for a view over the whole white valley. Lunch is at Supara Chunkurchak, a wooden restaurant with mountain views. Order what you like, lunch is not included.

A short horse ride in the snowy forest is possible, and beginners are welcome. We can also add a natural hot spring if you ask in advance, though it means a later return. At the end of the day we drive back and drop you at your hotel or anywhere in the city.

name: Issyk-Kul Winter Yurt & Canyons - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt
summary: Two winter days around Issyk-Kul in a private heated car. We climb Burana Tower, hike Konorchek Canyon in the snow and sleep in a heated yurt on the south shore. Day two brings Skazka Canyon and the frozen Barskoon waterfall. An eagle hunting show and a lakeshore ride can be added at extra cost. A short trip with both culture and nature.
highlights: Burana Tower, balbals and Chui Valley views
2 to 3 hour hike in snowy Konorchek Canyon
Night in a heated yurt on the Issyk-Kul shore
Skazka Canyon and the frozen Barskoon waterfall

blurb.hook: Red canyons in snow and a warm yurt by a lake that never freezes.
blurb.text: Burana Tower, the Konorchek and Skazka canyons, the frozen Barskoon waterfall and a night in a heated yurt by Issyk-Kul.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Bokonbayevo via Burana and Konorchek
desc: We pick you up at your hotel in the morning and head toward Issyk-Kul. Your guide runs through the plan as the city gives way to snowy mountains.

First stop is Burana Tower, a Silk Road landmark. Visit the small museum, walk among the old stone balbals and climb the tower for a view over the Chui Valley and the Tien Shan. In Boom Gorge we break for samovar tea, warm kattama bread and snacks.
Then comes the hike in Konorchek Canyon, 2 to 3 hours with your guide. Red rock and white snow make a strong contrast, and a viewpoint gives you a place to rest and take photos.

By late afternoon we reach a yurt camp on the south shore of Issyk-Kul. On request, a local hunter shows how Kyrgyz hunt with eagles. Dinner is home-cooked and served in the dining yurt. You sleep in your own heated yurt.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Skazka and Barskoon
desc: Breakfast is warm and served at the camp. If you asked for it, a 2-hour ride follows along the snowy shore of Issyk-Kul. The pace is easy, fine for beginners and experienced riders alike.
Next is Skazka Canyon, also called Fairy-Tale Canyon. You spend about an hour walking among its coloured rock shapes, which stand out sharply against the snow.

From there we drive up into Barskoon Gorge for a short winter walk to the frozen waterfall, between tall spruce and icy cliffs. A stop at a local hot spring is optional. Your guide checks the road and the weather and suggests the best one.
Then we turn back toward Bishkek, with lunch on the way. We drop you at your hotel or wherever suits you in the city.

name: Chong-Kemin & Issyk-Kul in Winter - 3 Days
accommodations: 1 night at guesthouse, 1 night at yurt
summary: Three winter days from Bishkek to Chong-Kemin and Issyk-Kul. Walk in snowy Ala-Archa, climb Burana Tower and spend a night with a local family in Chong-Kemin. Then ride a horse or take a horse-drawn carriage through the valley, see the Kok-Moinok canyons and an eagle hunting show, and sleep in a heated yurt by the lake. Easy routes, good for families.
highlights: Horse ride or carriage in snowy Chong-Kemin
Night with a local family in Chong-Kemin
Private eagle hunting show and archery in Bokonbayevo
Frozen waterfall in Barskoon Gorge

blurb.hook: Snowy valleys, a family guesthouse and a yurt by Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: Ala-Archa, Burana Tower, a winter ride in Chong-Kemin, the Kok-Moinok and Skazka canyons, an eagle show and the frozen Barskoon waterfall.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Ala-Archa and Burana
desc: We pick you up from your hotel in the morning and drive to Ala-Archa National Park. Snow sits on the trees and the river is frozen. On an easy forest walk you can feed the squirrels and birds.

Next is Burana Tower, a 9th-century minaret from Balasagun, a Silk Road city. Climb to the top for a winter view, look round the small museum and walk among the balbals, stone figures carved by nomads.
In the afternoon we drive to Chong-Kemin National Park. You stay with a local family in a warm guesthouse with private rooms and hot showers. Dinner is homemade.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Issyk-Kul via Kok-Moinok and Bokonbayevo
desc: After breakfast, choose how to see the snowy valley. A 2 to 3 hour horse ride suits active travellers. A traditional horse-drawn carriage is the calmer choice, good for families and anyone who would rather not ride. Both follow easy routes.
Then we drive to the Kok-Moinok canyons. The walk is short and takes almost no effort, and the coloured rock looks sharp under snow.
In the afternoon we reach Bokonbayevo for a private eagle hunting show. The golden eagle flies, lands and shows the old hunting techniques. You can take photos and try a short archery session.
In the evening we arrive at a yurt camp by the lake. Dinner is in a big yurt, and you sleep in your own heated yurt beside the quiet winter shore.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Skazka and Barskoon
desc: After breakfast we walk for about an hour in Skazka Canyon, among red rock shapes. Snow sets them off well for photos.
We continue to Barskoon Gorge and its frozen waterfall. A short walk brings you to the viewpoint, with fresh air and mountain views around you.
We stop for lunch on the road back and reach Bishkek in the evening.

name: Winter Issyk-Kul & Karakol Skiing - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt, 2 nights at hotel
activities: hiking - 2 days, skiing - 1 day, sightseeing - 1 day
summary: A winter loop around Issyk-Kul from Bishkek. We walk snowy red canyons, meet an eagle hunter in Bokonbayevo, see the frozen falls of Barskoon and the Seven Bulls at Jeti-Oguz, then give you a full day on the slopes at Karakol. It suits skiers and first-timers alike, plus anyone who wants the lake without summer crowds.
highlights: A full ski day at Karakol, with lessons for beginners
Frozen waterfalls in Barskoon Gorge
Eagle hunter demo and archery in Bokonbayevo
Snow on the red rocks of Skazka and Jeti-Oguz

blurb.hook: Snowy canyons, a golden eagle and a full day on Karakol's slopes.
blurb.text: Four winter days around Issyk-Kul: Burana Tower, frozen Barskoon falls, a yurt night, Karakol skiing and hot springs, then home along the north shore.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Bokonbayevo via Burana Tower and Boom Gorge
desc: We collect you from your Bishkek hotel and head east as the snowy ridges come into view. First stop is Burana Tower, an 11th-century Silk Road minaret. You see the stone balbals and the small museum, then climb up for a winter view over the Chui Valley.
In Boom Gorge we pull in at a roadside tea house. Hot tea from a samovar and fresh katama bread warm you up before the walk.

Then you pick your canyon with your guide. Konorchek Canyon is a moderate hike of about 3 hours between red sandstone walls. Kok-Moinok is an easy walk of about an hour. We decide together on the day, based on the snow and how you feel.
By afternoon we reach Bokonbayevo. A local berkutchi shows how he works with his golden eagle in winter. You can try archery and take photos with the bird. The night is spent in a yurt.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Karakol via Skazka, Barskoon and Jeti-Oguz
desc: Breakfast is served in the yurt, with Issyk-Kul quiet under winter light. Our first stop is Skazka Canyon. Snow makes its red and orange rock shapes stand out even more. Your guide walks you to the best viewpoints and tells the old stories behind them.
Next comes Barskoon Gorge. A short hike through spruce trees and snow leads to waterfalls frozen into ice. It is one of the best photo stops of the trip.

At Jeti-Oguz you see the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart rock, red cliffs dusted with white. There is time to walk further into the gorge. A horse ride on the snowy trails is possible here as an extra, and it suits beginners.
In the evening we reach Karakol. You check into a warm hotel and have dinner before tomorrow's ski day.

itinerary.title: Ski day at Karakol and hot springs
desc: After breakfast we drive up to Karakol Ski Resort, set among pine forest and high Tien Shan peaks. The whole day is yours on the mountain.

New to skiing? Rent gear on site and book a lesson with an instructor if you like. Confident skiers get longer runs and higher viewpoints. Kids have tubing, sledding and gentle slopes, and a panoramic cable car climbs above 3,000 meters for anyone who prefers to just look.
When the lifts close, we take you to a natural hot spring in Karakol. Warm mineral water after a cold day on the snow is the best way to rest your legs. Then back to the hotel for the night.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Bishkek via Grigoriev and Semyonov Gorges
desc: We start with Karakol itself. The Dungan Mosque was built without a single nail and has a bright Chinese-style look. The wooden Russian Orthodox Church, with its green roofs and fine carving, is the town's other landmark.

Then we drive to the north shore of Issyk-Kul and turn into Grigoriev and Semyonov Gorges. In winter you find snowy meadows, tall spruce and frozen rivers under white peaks. The walk here is easy, with plenty of time for photos.
From there we follow the quiet north shore road back to Bishkek, stopping for photos whenever you ask. We drop you at your hotel in the evening.

name: Issyk-Kul Canyons, Eagles & Yurt - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt
summary: Two days on the quiet south shore of Issyk-Kul. We hike Konorchek and Skazka canyons, hold a golden eagle in Bokonbayevo, ride horses by the lake and sleep in a yurt camp on the shore. It is a private trip with your own guide, and it fits travellers who have a short window but want more than a city break.
highlights: Hike the red sandstone walls of Konorchek Canyon
Hold a golden eagle at a live hunting show
Ride 1-2 hours on the lakeshore or in the hills
A night in a yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore

blurb.hook: Red canyons, a golden eagle and a yurt night by Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: A private two-day loop from Bishkek: Burana Tower, Konorchek and Skazka canyons, an eagle show, a lakeside ride and the Barskoon waterfall.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Bokonbayevo via Burana Tower and Konorchek Canyon
desc: Your guide meets you in the hotel lobby, talks you through the day and drives you in a private air-conditioned car. It is just your group and us.

First stop is Burana Tower, a Silk Road minaret from the 9th to 10th century. You walk through the small archaeology museum and past the old stone balbals. Then you climb the tower for a view of the Tien Shan.

Next we drive into Boom Gorge to Konorchek Canyon. The hike takes 2 to 3 hours along narrow paths between red and orange cliffs, and you do not need special fitness. It ends at a high point above the whole canyon.

In the evening we reach a yurt camp on the south shore. A champion berkutchi shows how he hunts with his golden eagle, and then the bird sits on your arm. Dinner is home-cooked: fresh bread, hot soup and slow-cooked meat.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Barskoon and Skazka Canyon
desc: Breakfast is in the dining yurt by the water. After it, a local horseman gives you a short briefing and stays with you the whole ride. No experience is needed.
You choose the route. Ride along the shore with the blue lake beside you, or climb into the hills for a view over the lake and valley. The ride lasts 1 to 2 hours.
Then we drive to Barskoon. Take the easy 30-minute walk to the lower viewpoint, or the 3-hour hike to the upper waterfall. Your guide comes along either way.
Lunch is at a local cafe near Skazka Canyon. Afterwards you get about an hour among its red and gold rocks, carved by wind. In the afternoon we drive back and drop you at your hotel in Bishkek.

name: Song-Kul Yurt Night by Car & Horse - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt
summary: We drive you from Bishkek to Song-Kul at 3,016 meters over the Kalmak-Ashuu Pass, with stops at Burana Tower and Kochkor. You sleep in a yurt on the shore, ride across the jailoo in the morning, then return over 33 Parrots Pass with a hidden waterfall and an Issyk-Kul beach on the way. A private trip that suits riders of any level.
highlights: Kalmak-Ashuu Pass on the drive up to Song-Kul
A yurt night at 3,016 meters under the Milky Way
Morning ride on the jailoo, fine for beginners
33 Parrots Pass and a beach stop at Issyk-Kul

blurb.hook: Song-Kul in one night, by car over two passes, with a ride on the jailoo.
blurb.text: A private two-day trip: Burana Tower, the Kalmak-Ashuu climb, a yurt by the lake, a morning ride, then 33 Parrots Pass and an Issyk-Kul beach.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Song-Kul via Burana Tower, Kochkor and Kalmak-Ashuu
desc: Your guide picks you up at your hotel in the morning. We stop first at Burana Tower, a Silk Road minaret from the 9th to 10th century with old balbal stones around it. You hear its story and climb up for a view of the Tien Shan.
In Boom Gorge we break for kattama, a flaky layered bread, with tea from an old samovar. A short stop in Kochkor follows, and then the road starts to climb.
The Kalmak-Ashuu Pass is one of our favourite drives. Rock turns into green hills and yaks graze in the distance. We stop at the top so you can get out and take photos.
You reach the yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore around 5 pm. Dinner is home-cooked. Afterwards, step outside: at this height, with almost no light around, the Milky Way is plain to see.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Song-Kul to Bishkek via 33 Parrots Pass and Issyk-Kul
desc: After breakfast in the yurt you ride out across the open pastures around the lake. A local horseman rides beside you, so beginners are welcome.
Around 11 am we start back over 33 Parrots Pass, a road of tight bends and wide views. We stop at the best viewpoints, then take a short walk to a quiet waterfall near Song-Kul that few people know.
On the way down we stop at an Issyk-Kul beach so you can rest by the water. Lunch is at a local cafe on the road. We drop you at your Bishkek hotel in the evening, around 7 to 8 pm.

name: Kara-Kiya Pass Ride to Song-Kul - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt
summary: A short, full-on ride for confident riders. We drive you to Kyzart, put you in the saddle in Kilemche valley and cross the Kara-Kiya Pass at 3,400 meters to reach Song-Kul by evening. You sleep in a lakeside yurt and ride back by another pass the next day. It runs all year, and summer brings green jailoo full of herds.
highlights: Over the Kara-Kiya Pass at 3,400 meters on horseback
Ride in from Kilemche valley on a herders' trail
A yurt night on the Song-Kul shore under clear skies
Back by a different pass, so no trail repeats

blurb.hook: Song-Kul on horseback in two days, any month of the year.
blurb.text: For confident riders short on time: 4 to 5 hours in the saddle over the Kara-Kiya Pass to a lakeside yurt, then a new route back to Kyzart.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Kyzart, ride over Kara-Kiya Pass to Song-Kul
desc: We pick you up early at your Bishkek hotel. The drive south into Naryn region takes 4 to 5 hours and passes the Orto-Tokoy reservoir as the mountains open up.
From Kyzart village it is a short hop up to Kilemche valley, where the horses and horsemen are ready. You mount up and go.
The trail climbs straight away, through open grass to the Kara-Kiya Pass at 3,400 meters. It is windy on top and the view runs far in every direction. Riding time is about 4 to 5 hours.
You come down to Song-Kul as the evening light hits the lake. Dinner is served in the yurt, and outside it is completely quiet.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Song-Kul to Kyzart on horseback and back to Bishkek
desc: Get up before breakfast if you can. Mist on the water, horses on the jailoo and the last stars are worth the early start.
After breakfast you ride out by a different pass, so the views are new all the way down. The trail drops into Kilemche valley and flattens out near Kyzart. Riding time is about 3 to 4 hours.
Lunch waits at a local guesthouse in Kyzart. Then our driver takes you the 4 to 5 hours back to your hotel in Bishkek.

name: Song-Kul Two-Pass Loop on Horseback - 3 Days
accommodations: 1 night at shepherd's house, 1 night at yurt
summary: A true loop to Song-Kul from Kyzart: in over the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass, out over the Kara-Kiya Pass, both at 3,400 meters. The first night is in a working shepherd's house in Kilemche, the second in a yurt on the lake. Beginners are welcome, our guide rides with you all three days, and the trek runs all year round.
highlights: Two different passes at 3,400 meters, no backtracking
A night with herders in a shepherd's house in Kilemche
A yurt on the Song-Kul shore with the Milky Way above
Open to beginners, with a gallop lesson if you want

blurb.hook: In by one pass, out by another: a three-day loop to Song-Kul.
blurb.text: Ride from Kyzart to a shepherd's house in Kilemche, over Jalgyz-Karagai to a lakeside yurt, and home via the Kara-Kiya Pass. Any level, any season.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Kyzart, ride to Kilemche
desc: We pick you up early in Bishkek for the 4 to 5 hour drive into Naryn Province. The road passes the Orto-Tokoy reservoir as the ridges close in.
In Kyzart you meet your guides and have lunch with a local family. Then the horses are saddled and the afternoon ride begins.

The trail rises slowly up an open valley into the mountains. After 3 to 4 hours you reach Kilemche and a shepherd's house. This is a real herders' home, not a guesthouse for visitors. Dinner is served there, and the altitude sends you to sleep early.

itinerary.title: Kilemche over Jalgyz-Karagai Pass to Song-Kul
desc: After breakfast with the shepherd's family, today's big climb starts. The trail heads up through open alpine ground to the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass at 3,400 meters. Below you, the valleys fill with horses, sheep and cattle.
From the top, Song-Kul lies wide and blue, with no towns on its banks. You ride down through summer herding grounds and reach the yurt camp in the early afternoon.
There is time to walk by the water or rest. Dinner is in the yurt, and after dark the Milky Way crosses the whole sky above the lake.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Song-Kul over Kara-Kiya Pass to Kyzart and Bishkek
desc: Step out before breakfast to see mist on the lake and horses grazing as the stars fade.

The last ride takes a new line. You climb to the Kara-Kiya Pass at 3,400 meters and drop back toward Kyzart, so the scenery is fresh all day. By now you will feel at home in the saddle, and if you are ready, your guide will show you how to gallop.
Lunch is at a guesthouse in Kyzart. Our driver then takes you the 4 to 5 hours back to your Bishkek hotel.

name: Two Nights at Song-Kul on Horseback - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at shepherd's house, 2 nights at yurt
summary: Most treks touch Song-Kul and turn back. This one stays two nights at the lake, in two different yurt camps. You ride from Kyzart via Kilemche and the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass, follow the shore to Kara-Kiya valley with a free afternoon to swim or rest, and leave over the Kara-Kiya Pass. Short riding days make it right for any level.
highlights: Two nights by Song-Kul in two different yurt camps
A shoreline ride to Kara-Kiya valley
A free afternoon to swim, walk or join herding life
Two passes at 3,400 meters, in and out by new trails

blurb.hook: Don't just reach Song-Kul. Stay two nights and ride its shore.
blurb.text: Four days in the saddle at an easy pace: a shepherd's house in Kilemche, two lakeside yurt camps, a free afternoon by the water and two high passes.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Kyzart, ride to Kilemche
desc: We pick you up early from your hotel for the 4 to 5 hour drive south into Naryn Province, past the Orto-Tokoy reservoir.
In Kyzart village you meet your guides over lunch with a local family. Then you mount up and ride gently up the valley toward Kilemche at 2,500 meters, about 3 to 4 hours in the saddle.
The night is in a shepherd's house, a working highland home rather than a guesthouse. Dinner is served there.

itinerary.title: Kilemche over Jalgyz-Karagai Pass to Song-Kul
desc: After breakfast you take on the main climb of the trek, the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass at 3,400 meters. The trail goes up steadily through open alpine country, with herds grazing in the valleys below.
At the top, Song-Kul opens out in front of you, wide and still, with no towns on the shore. Riding time is about 3 hours, and you reach the first yurt camp by early afternoon.
Dinner is in the yurt. When it gets dark, the Milky Way spans the sky from one ridge to the other.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Lakeshore ride to Kara-Kiya valley
desc: Today the lake is the whole point. You ride along the Song-Kul shore with water on one side and rolling hills on the other, for about 2 to 3 hours.
The second yurt camp sits in Kara-Kiya valley. A local nomad family serves lunch.
The afternoon is free. Swim if the day is warm, walk the pastures, help the families with their daily work or just sit by the water. Dinner and the night are in a yurt on the shore.

itinerary.title: Kara-Kiya Pass to Kyzart and back to Bishkek
desc: Get up early for mist on the lake and horses on the jailoo as the stars go out.
After breakfast you climb to the Kara-Kiya Pass at 3,400 meters. Look back for Song-Kul and ahead into the Jumgal valley. Then the trail drops steadily to Kyzart over 4 to 5 hours of riding.
Lunch waits at a guesthouse in Kyzart. Our driver then takes you the 4 to 5 hours back to your hotel in Bishkek.

name: Song-Kul on Horseback & Issyk-Kul - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at shepherd's house, 2 nights at yurt
summary: Two lakes in four days. You ride for three days from Kyzart over two 3,400-meter passes to Song-Kul, sleeping with herders in Kilemche and in a lakeside yurt. Then we drive you to the south shore of Issyk-Kul for an eagle show, Skazka Canyon and the Barskoon waterfall. Any riding level is fine, and it runs all year.
highlights: Three days riding from Kyzart to Song-Kul and back
A night in a shepherd's house at 2,500 meters
Golden eagle show on the Issyk-Kul south shore
Skazka Canyon and the Barskoon waterfall hike

blurb.hook: Three days in the saddle to Song-Kul, then a day on Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: Ride over two high passes to a Song-Kul yurt, sleep by Issyk-Kul, then meet a berkutchi and walk Skazka Canyon and Barskoon Gorge on the way home.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Kyzart, ride to Kilemche
desc: We collect you early from your Bishkek hotel. The 4 to 5 hour drive heads south into Naryn Province and passes the wide Orto-Tokoy reservoir, where the real mountains begin.
Around midday you reach Kyzart and sit down to a home-cooked lunch at a local guesthouse. Then you meet your horses. Your guide shows you how to sit, steer and stop before you set off.
The trail climbs gently through green valleys. After 3 to 4 hours you arrive in Kilemche, a meadow at 2,500 meters. You stay the night with a shepherd family in a simple home, with a warm dinner.

itinerary.title: Kilemche over Jalgyz-Karagai Pass to Song-Kul
desc: After breakfast with the shepherd's family, you ride up to the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass at 3,400 meters. Your guide stays with the group the whole way and sets an easy pace.
As you climb, thousands of horses, sheep and cattle graze in the valleys below. From the top you get your first look at Song-Kul, huge and calm, with nothing on its shore to block the view.
You reach the yurt camp in the early afternoon, with time to walk along the water. Dinner is in the yurt, and with no city lights for miles, the Milky Way fills the night sky.
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Song-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Song-Kul over Kara-Kiya Pass to Kyzart and Issyk-Kul
desc: Wake early for mist on the lake and horses grazing as the last stars fade. Breakfast is in the yurt, with no rush.
Your final ride crosses the Kara-Kiya Pass, a different trail from the way in. From the top you see Song-Kul behind you and the open valley ahead. The ride down to Kyzart takes 2 to 3 hours.

A farewell lunch at a Kyzart guesthouse ends the trek. Then we drive you 2 to 3 hours down to the south shore of Issyk-Kul, one of the largest lakes in the world. The night is in a yurt camp by the water.
itinerary.transfer: Kyzart to Issyk-Kul south shore · 2-3 h
itinerary.overnight: Yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore

itinerary.title: Eagle show, Skazka Canyon and Barskoon Gorge, then Bishkek
desc: The morning starts with a berkutchi, a Kyrgyz eagle hunter. He shows how golden eagles have been trained to hunt here for more than a thousand years. You can hold the bird and take photos with him.
Next is Skazka Canyon, whose name means fairy tale in Russian. Wind and rain have shaped its red and orange walls into strange forms. A short walk takes you inside, with views over Issyk-Kul.
Then we hike to the waterfall in Barskoon Gorge, a narrow rocky valley in the forest. Yuri Gagarin, the first man in space, liked to rest here.
From Barskoon we drive back along the south shore, about 4 to 5 hours with mountains in view. You are at your Bishkek hotel by early evening, around 7 to 8 pm.
itinerary.activity: Eagle show · Canyon walk · Waterfall hike

name: Song-Kul Ride & Issyk-Kul Circle - 5 Days
accommodations: 1 night at shepherd's house, 2 nights at yurt, 1 night at hotel
summary: Three days in the saddle from Kyzart over two passes to Song-Kul and back, with a night in a shepherd's house and one in a yurt by the lake. Then we drive you to Issyk-Kul for an eagle show, Skazka Canyon, Barskoon Gorge, Jeti-Oguz and Karakol, ending with a boat ride and hot springs. Made for riders who want the high pastures and the big lake in one trip.
highlights: Ride over Jalgyz Karagai Pass, 3,400 m, to Song-Kul
Night in a shepherd's house at Kilemche, 2,500 m
Golden eagle show with a berkutchi in Bokonbayevo
Skazka, Barskoon waterfall, Jeti-Oguz and Karakol

blurb.hook: Three days on horseback to Song-Kul, then a full circle of Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: Ride from Kyzart to Song-Kul over two high passes and sleep in a yurt by the water. Then drive both shores of Issyk-Kul, from an eagle show to hot springs.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Kilemche Valley via Kyzart
desc: We pick you up at your Bishkek hotel early. The drive south into Naryn Region takes four to five hours. Once you pass the Orto Tokoy reservoir, the real mountains begin.
Lunch is at a guesthouse in Kyzart, your first home-cooked Kyrgyz meal. Then you meet your horses and your English-speaking guide. A short lesson covers how to sit, steer and stop.
The trail rises slowly through green valleys and open grass. After three to four hours you reach Kilemche, a meadow at 2,500 m. You sleep in a shepherd's house, and dinner is cooked right there.

itinerary.title: Kilemche to Song-Kul over Jalgyz Karagai Pass
desc: Breakfast at the shepherd's house, then back in the saddle. Today is the big climb, up to Jalgyz Karagai Pass at 3,400 m. Your guide rides with the group all the way and keeps the pace comfortable.

Higher up, the valleys below fill with horses, sheep and cattle grazing loose. From the pass you get your first look at Song-Kul. No towns stand on its shore, just water and open grass in every direction.
You ride down to the yurt camp by early afternoon and have time to walk along the lake. Dinner is served inside the yurt. With no lights anywhere around, the Milky Way crosses the whole sky.

itinerary.title: Song-Kul to Bokonbayevo via Kara Kiya Pass
desc: Get up early if you can. Mist sits on the water, horses graze by the camp and the last stars fade. Breakfast is in the yurt, with no rush.
Your last ride takes a different way out, over Kara Kiya Pass. From the top you see Song-Kul behind you and a wide valley ahead. The descent to Kyzart takes two to three hours.
A farewell lunch in Kyzart closes the trek. Your driver and guide for the lake part meet you there. About two hours by car bring you down to the south shore of Issyk-Kul.

In Bokonbayevo a local berkutchi flies his golden eagle for you, and you can hold the bird for photos. Then you check in at the yurt camp and eat dinner in the dining yurt. A luxury yurt with its own toilet and shower can be arranged.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Karakol along the south shore
desc: Today is all south shore. First comes Skazka Canyon, also called Fairy Tale Canyon, where wind and rain worked red and orange rock into strange shapes. A short walk takes you inside, with Issyk-Kul in view.
Next is Barskoon Gorge, a narrow rocky valley with forest on its slopes. You hike up to the waterfall. Yuri Gagarin, the first man in space, liked to come here.

In the afternoon we drive east to Jeti-Oguz, the Seven Bulls, named for the red rocks above a wide green valley. It is one of the most photographed spots in the country, and a short walk shows you why.
The day ends in Karakol, the largest town in eastern Kyrgyzstan, at the foot of the Tien Shan. You check in at a hotel and can stroll the streets in the evening.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Bishkek via Cholpon-Ata
desc: The morning starts with a walk around Karakol. You see the Dungan Mosque, built of wood in 1910 without a single nail, and the Russian Orthodox church with its green roof. Then the central bazaar, a good place for souvenirs.
Next we drive up into the Semenov and Grigoriev gorges. Both have glacial rivers, pine forest and wide mountain views. You get time for a walk.
Along the north shore we reach Cholpon-Ata. You visit the Ruh Ordo complex by the water, take a boat out on the lake and soak in natural hot springs.
The last drive to Bishkek takes four to five hours. You are back at your hotel in the early evening.

name: Burana, Chong-Kemin & Cholpon-Ata - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at guesthouse
summary: A private two-day trip east of Bishkek for travellers short on time. You climb Burana Tower, walk to the Kegety waterfall and spend the afternoon in Chong-Kemin on horseback, in a horse carriage or on foot. Day two takes you through Kok-Moynok Canyons to Cholpon-Ata on Issyk-Kul for petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, a boat ride and hot springs.
highlights: Climb Burana Tower, a 9th to 10th century Silk Road site
2-3 hour ride through the meadows of Chong-Kemin
Red and purple rock of Kok-Moynok Canyons on foot
Petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, a boat ride and hot springs

blurb.hook: One tower, one valley, one lake: three landscapes in two days.
blurb.text: Ride or hike in Chong-Kemin and sleep at a family guesthouse. Then walk Kok-Moynok Canyons and spend the afternoon at Cholpon-Ata on Issyk-Kul.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Burana Tower and Kegety Gorge
desc: Your guide collects you from your Bishkek hotel and we head east. The first stop is Burana Tower, built in the 9th to 10th centuries on the Silk Road. You walk past the old balbal stone figures, then climb the tower for a view toward the Tien Shan.
Next is Kegety Gorge, with a clear river and forest on the slopes. A short walk brings you close to the Kegety waterfall. It is a good place to stretch your legs.

By early afternoon you reach Chong-Kemin National Park and a family-run guesthouse. Lunch is home-cooked. Then you pick your afternoon: a 2-3 hour guided ride through meadows and easy trails, a horse carriage ride that suits families, or a hike.
Dinner is homemade too. A sauna and a swimming pool are available for an extra fee. The valley is quiet at night and the sky is full of stars.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Cholpon-Ata and back to Bishkek
desc: After breakfast we drive east through Boom Gorge, where the Chu River runs between high stone walls. It is worth a photo stop.
At Kok-Moynok Canyons you walk among red, orange and purple rock. The ground is easy and an hour is plenty. Take your time with the camera.

We carry on to Issyk-Kul and lunch in Cholpon-Ata. You visit Ruh Ordo, a lakeside complex devoted to the world's religions and cultures, and the petroglyphs, carved more than 3,000 years ago. From May to September, weather allowing, you take a short boat ride and relax in natural hot springs.
Late in the afternoon we drive back to Bishkek and arrive in the evening.
itinerary.transfer: Chong-Kemin to Cholpon-Ata to Bishkek · 350 km · 5-6 h
itinerary.activity: Canyon walk · 1 h · Boat ride · Hot springs

name: Konorchek Hike & Chong-Kemin Ride - 2 Days
accommodations: 1 night at guesthouse
summary: A private two-day trip for people who would rather be outdoors than in town. After Burana Tower and the Kegety waterfall, you ride through the meadows of Chong-Kemin and sleep at a family guesthouse. Next morning you hike two to three hours through the red rock of Konorchek Canyon, with an optional lakeside lunch at Balykchy on the way home.
highlights: Ride the open meadows of Chong-Kemin National Park
2-3 hour hike through Konorchek Canyon's red rock
Kegety waterfall and the old Burana Tower
Optional beach walk and lunch at Balykchy on Issyk-Kul

blurb.hook: A day in the saddle, then a morning among red canyon walls.
blurb.text: Ride in Chong-Kemin and sleep at a family guesthouse, then hike Konorchek Canyon. Finish with a lake stop at Balykchy or head straight back to Bishkek.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Burana and Kegety
desc: We meet you at your hotel in Bishkek and drive east. Burana Tower comes first, a Silk Road minaret from the 9th to 10th centuries. Your guide tells its story among the balbal stones, and you can climb up for a view of the Tien Shan.
In Kegety Gorge a short walk leads to the waterfall. The river is clear and the slopes are covered in forest.

Early in the afternoon you arrive at a family guesthouse in Chong-Kemin National Park, where lunch is waiting. Many consider this valley the best place to ride in Kyrgyzstan. You head out for 2-3 hours across meadows and gentle trails, or choose a horse carriage or a hike instead.
Dinner is cooked at home. Sauna and pool are optional, at extra cost.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Konorchek Canyon and Bishkek
desc: After breakfast we drive out through Boom Gorge, a tight canyon cut by the Chu River. We stop briefly for photos.

At Konorchek Canyon you set off on foot. Wind and water carved the red, orange and purple rock into towers and ridges. The hike is easy to moderate and takes 2 to 3 hours at a calm pace. Some travellers say it looks like Mars.

After the hike you choose how to finish. With time to spare, we stop in Balykchy at the western tip of Issyk-Kul for a walk on the beach and lunch by the lake. If you need to be back sooner, we eat on the road and drive straight to Bishkek.
Either way, you are in Bishkek by early evening.
itinerary.transfer: Chong-Kemin to Bishkek via Konorchek · 200 km · 3-4 h

name: Chong-Kemin, Eagle Show & Lake Yurt - 3 Days
accommodations: 1 night at guesthouse, 1 night at yurt
summary: Three private days from Bishkek to the south shore of Issyk-Kul. You ride in Chong-Kemin, hike a canyon of your choice, meet an eagle hunter in Bokonbayevo and sleep in a yurt by the lake. On the way home you walk through Skazka Canyon and picnic by the Barskoon waterfall. A good fit if you want riding, culture and canyons in a short trip.
highlights: Ride, hike or take a horse carriage in Chong-Kemin
Hold a golden eagle and try archery in Bokonbayevo
Night in a yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore
Picnic lunch by the Barskoon waterfall

blurb.hook: Horses in Chong-Kemin, an eagle hunter and a night in a lakeside yurt.
blurb.text: Burana Tower and a ride in Chong-Kemin, then a canyon hike, a private eagle show with archery and a yurt by Issyk-Kul. Skazka and Barskoon on the way home.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Burana Tower
desc: Your guide picks you up in Bishkek and we drive east to Burana Tower. It dates from the 9th to 10th centuries and stands among old balbal stone figures. Climb the steps for a wide view of the Tien Shan.
We continue to Kegety Gorge and walk a short way to its waterfall. Forest, a clear river and cool air make it a good first stop in the mountains.

In the early afternoon you check in at a family guesthouse in Chong-Kemin National Park and sit down to a home-cooked lunch. Later you choose: 2-3 hours on horseback through meadows and easy trails, a horse carriage ride, or a walk.
Dinner is homemade. You can add the sauna or pool for a fee.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Bokonbayevo via the canyons
desc: After breakfast we drive toward Issyk-Kul with mountains on both sides. The first stop is a canyon, and you pick which one.

Kok-Moynok is a gentle one-hour walk through pink and red rock with views of the lake. Konorchek is a 2 to 3 hour hike into deep red gorges with steep walls. Your guide helps you choose based on how much you want to walk.
Lunch is in Balykchy, a quiet town at the western end of the lake. In the afternoon we reach Bokonbayevo for a private show with a burkutchi, a Kyrgyz eagle hunter.

His golden eagle flies out over open ground and comes back to his glove. Your guide translates as he explains how the birds are trained and what they mean to his family. You can hold the eagle, then try a traditional archery lesson, which is harder than it looks. At sunset you reach the yurt camp on the lake, with dinner in the main yurt.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Skazka and Barskoon
desc: After breakfast in the yurt we head east along the south shore. Skazka Canyon, also called Fairy Tale Canyon, is a short drive from camp.
Its red, orange and yellow rock has worn into towers that look like castles and animals. A one-hour walk on an easy path takes you through the middle of it, with no steep parts.
Further east we follow a river into Barskoon Gorge, between forest and high cliffs. A short walk brings you to the foot of the waterfall, and lunch is a picnic by the river.
After lunch we start the long drive back to Bishkek, partly along the north shore. You are at your hotel in the evening.

name: Song-Kul & 33 Parrots Pass Express - 3 Days
accommodations: 2 nights at yurt
summary: Two lakes in three days, with a yurt night at each. We drive over Kalmak-Ashuu Pass to Song-Kul at 3,000 m, you ride its summer pastures next morning, then we come down 33 Parrots Pass to an eagle hunter and a camp on Issyk-Kul. The last day takes in Barskoon Gorge and Skazka Canyon. The drives are long, so it suits travellers who want a lot in little time.
highlights: Yurt night at Song-Kul, 3,000 m up
Ride the summer pastures around Song-Kul
Down 33 Parrots Pass to a hidden waterfall
Barskoon waterfalls and Skazka Canyon on the last day

blurb.hook: Song-Kul and Issyk-Kul in three days, sleeping in a yurt at both.
blurb.text: Climb to Song-Kul via Kalmak-Ashuu, ride at 3,000 m, then take 33 Parrots Pass down to an eagle show and a yurt by Issyk-Kul. Summer only.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Song-Kul via Burana and Kok-Moynok
desc: Your guide meets you at your hotel in the morning and we drive east. At Burana Tower you hear about the old city of Balasagun and the balbal stones around it. A narrow staircase leads to the top and a view of the Tien Shan.
The land turns dry and colourful at Kok-Moynok Canyons. You walk for about 30 minutes, an easy stroll with time for photos. Lunch is in Kochkor village.

In the afternoon the road climbs over Kalmak-Ashuu Pass. The air cools and wide pastures with grazing herds open up. By late afternoon you reach the yurt camp at Song-Kul, 3,000 m up, for dinner under a clear sky.

itinerary.title: Song-Kul to Bokonbayevo via 33 Parrots Pass
desc: The morning is yours. Take a gentle ride across the pastures, fine for beginners, or walk the shore and watch herders with their animals. Every summer nomad families bring their flocks up to these meadows.

Mid-morning we leave the lake on 33 Parrots Pass, a road of tight bends with stops for photos. At the bottom an easy 30-minute walk leads to a hidden waterfall in a shady gorge. Then we follow the south shore of Issyk-Kul.
In the afternoon you meet a local eagle hunter. He explains how the birds are trained and how the tradition survives today. You can hold the eagle yourself.
You spend the night at a yurt camp by the lake, with a home-cooked dinner and a bonfire.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Barskoon and Skazka
desc: The morning is slow. You can add a horse ride in the hills or along the shore, paid on the spot, or just sit by the water. We set off late in the morning.
Barskoon Gorge is wide and green, with spruce on the slopes and a clear river. Walk 30 minutes to the first waterfall, or hike about 3 hours to a higher one further up the valley.
Skazka Canyon, the Fairy Tale Canyon, comes next. You spend about an hour among red, orange and ochre rock that looks like a ruined city. Your guide knows where the light is best for photos.
Late in the afternoon we drive back to Bishkek along the north shore, with the lake in view most of the way. You reach your hotel in the early evening.

name: Issyk-Kul Shore Ride, Eagles & Boat - 3 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt, 1 night at hotel
activities: hiking - 1 day, horse riding - 1 day, sightseeing - 1 day
summary: A full loop of Issyk-Kul in three private days. You start with Burana Tower and Konorchek Canyon, meet an eagle hunter in Bokonbayevo and sleep in a yurt near the shore. Then come a short beginner ride, Skazka Canyon, Barskoon, Jeti-Oguz and a night in Karakol, before Cholpon-Ata and a boat on the lake. For travellers who want the whole lake at a brisk pace.
highlights: Optional 2-3 hour hike in Konorchek Canyon
Eagle hunting show and a yurt night in Bokonbayevo
Beginner ride in the hills or along the lakeshore
Karakol's wooden Dungan Mosque and a lake boat ride

blurb.hook: Round the whole lake: eagle, yurt, horse, canyon and boat.
blurb.text: Three days that circle Issyk-Kul, from Konorchek and Skazka to Jeti-Oguz and Karakol, with a yurt night, a short ride and hot springs.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Bokonbayevo via Burana and Konorchek
desc: We pick you up in Bishkek in the morning and drive toward Issyk-Kul as the Tien Shan rises ahead. At Burana Tower, a Silk Road site from the 9th to 10th centuries, your guide tells the story of Balasagun among the balbal stones. Then you climb the tower for the view.
If you want some action, we stop at Konorchek Canyon for a 2-3 hour hike through red rock. It is scenic and not hard. If you would rather take it easy, we skip it and you get more time by the lake.
In the afternoon you reach Bokonbayevo. A local hunter explains why golden eagles mattered so much to nomads, then lets his bird fly across open ground.
