In the evening you check in at a yurt camp near the lake. Dinner is homemade Kyrgyz food, and the day ends around a bonfire.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Karakol via Skazka, Barskoon and Jeti-Oguz
desc: After breakfast at the yurt you go for a short ride, on mountain trails or by the water. It is gentle and fine for first-timers.

Next is Skazka Canyon, the Fairy Tale Canyon, all red and orange rock. An easy walk with your guide takes you to the best viewpoints. Then we turn into Barskoon Gorge and hike a forest trail to one of its waterfalls.
In the afternoon you see Jeti-Oguz, the Seven Bulls, and hear the legends behind its red cliffs. You can finish in natural hot springs before we reach Karakol for dinner and a hotel night.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Bishkek via Grigoriev Gorge and Cholpon-Ata
desc: We start with a short walk around Karakol. You visit the wooden Dungan Mosque, built in Chinese style without nails, and the Holy Trinity Orthodox Cathedral. Your guide explains how different peoples shaped the town.
Then we drive to the Grigoriev and Semenov gorges, with pine forest, rivers and open meadows. There is time for an easy walk. A short ride can be added at extra cost.
In Cholpon-Ata you visit the Ruh Ordo cultural centre by the lake and the petroglyphs, carved more than 2,000 years ago. From May to September you also take a boat out on the lake and can swim.
Then we drive home along the north shore and drop you at your hotel in the evening.

name: Karakol, Cholpon-Ata & Chong-Kemin - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt, 1 night at hotel, 1 night at guesthouse
summary: Four private days that circle Issyk-Kul and end in the green Chong-Kemin valley. You see Burana Tower, an eagle show and a yurt camp on the south shore, then Skazka, Barskoon, Jeti-Oguz and Karakol. The last night is at a family guesthouse, where you bake boorsok in the morning and ride before heading home. A softer pace, with choices built into every day.
highlights: Bake boorsok for breakfast at a Chong-Kemin guesthouse
Eagle show and a yurt night on the south shore
Skazka, Barskoon waterfalls and Jeti-Oguz in one day
2-3 hour ride through Chong-Kemin on the last day

blurb.hook: Circle Issyk-Kul, then slow down in Chong-Kemin with fresh boorsok.
blurb.text: An eagle and a yurt in Bokonbayevo, canyons and red cliffs on the way to Karakol, a boat on the lake, then a quiet last night in Chong-Kemin.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to the south shore via Burana Tower
desc: Your guide picks you up at your Bishkek hotel and we set off for Issyk-Kul. At Burana Tower you walk among the balbal stones and climb up for a wide view of the Tien Shan.
Further east there is an optional stop at Konorchek Canyon. The easy hike through red rock takes about 2 to 3 hours. Skip it if you would rather reach the lake earlier.
In the afternoon, on the south shore, you meet a golden eagle and its hunter. You learn how the old tradition works and get your photos with the bird.
In the evening you check in at a yurt camp by the lake. After dinner there is a bonfire.

itinerary.title: South shore canyons and gorges to Karakol
desc: After breakfast we follow the south shore east. First is Fairy Tale Canyon, also known as Skazka, where wind shaped red sandstone into castles, animals and walls. Your guide walks you to the best photo spots.
In Barskoon Gorge, among pine forest and peaks, a short hike takes you to the waterfalls fed by glacier water. We go at your pace.
After lunch we reach Jeti-Oguz and its famous red rocks, the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart. Take a relaxed walk, or add a horse ride toward Kok-Jaiyk Valley.
In the evening you check in at a hotel in Karakol. On request we stop at natural hot springs before dinner.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Chong-Kemin via Cholpon-Ata
desc: The morning is a short tour of Karakol. You see the Dungan Mosque, built in Chinese style without nails, and the wooden Russian Orthodox church. If you like, we add the local museum and its story of the town's Russian and Chinese communities.
We then drive along the north shore and stop in the Semenov and Grigoriev gorges for short walks and photos.
Lunch is at a lakeside restaurant in Cholpon-Ata. Then you visit Ruh Ordo and the open-air petroglyphs, and take a boat out on the lake, with life jackets for a swim. Hot springs can be added too.
In the afternoon we drive on to Chong-Kemin and a family-run guesthouse. Dinner is home-style and the evening is quiet.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Bishkek
desc: The day starts with a boorsok class. You make this traditional Kyrgyz bread with your hosts and eat it warm at breakfast.
Then pick one activity: a hike into the forest, a 2-3 hour guided ride through the valley or by the river, or a horse carriage ride.
Traditional horse games such as Kok-Boru, horse wrestling, Tyin Enmei or Kyz Kuumai can be arranged at extra cost. Rafting is possible as well.
In the afternoon we drive back to Bishkek and drop you at your hotel or the airport.

name: Issyk-Kul Full Circle & Boat Ride - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt, 2 nights at hotel
summary: A private four-day loop around Issyk-Kul with your own guide. You climb Burana Tower, watch a golden eagle fly to its hunter near Bokonbayevo and sleep in a yurt by the lake. Then come Skazka Canyon, the Barskoon waterfalls, the red cliffs of Jeti-Oguz and an army off-roader up to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs. A boat ride from Cholpon-Ata closes the trip.
highlights: Golden eagle show on the south shore near Bokonbayevo
A night in a lakeside yurt camp on Issyk-Kul
Off-road truck ride up to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs
Boat ride on Issyk-Kul from Cholpon-Ata

blurb.hook: One loop around Issyk-Kul, from Burana Tower to a boat on the lake.
blurb.text: Eagles near Bokonbayevo, a yurt by the water, red canyons, Altyn-Arashan by army truck and the north shore on the way home. Private and run all year.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Bokonbayevo via Burana Tower
desc: We collect you from your hotel in Bishkek and head east. First stop is Burana Tower, an old Silk Road minaret. Your guide tells its story, then you climb up for a wide view of the Chuy Valley and the Tien Shan.
Further on, Konorchek Canyon is an optional stop. If you like a short walk, we explore its red rock walls on foot. If not, we drive straight on to the lake.
In the afternoon we reach the south shore of Issyk-Kul near Bokonbayevo. A local hunter shows how he trains and flies his golden eagle. You can hold the bird for a photo.
The night is in a yurt camp by the lake. Dinner looks out over the water, and the evening ends around a bonfire.

itinerary.title: Skazka Canyon, Barskoon and Jeti-Oguz to Karakol
desc: After breakfast we walk into Skazka Canyon, also called Fairytale Canyon. Wind and rain have cut the red sandstone into walls, towers and shapes like dragons. The walk is easy, and your guide knows the best photo spots.
Next is Barskoon Gorge, with pine forest and peaks on both sides. You hike up to the Barskoon waterfalls, where glacier water drops down a steep cliff.

After lunch we drive into Jeti-Oguz Gorge to see the red cliffs called the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart. You can walk the valley at an easy pace. A horse ride up to Kok-Jaiyk Valley can be added if you want more.
In the evening we reach Karakol. If you like, we stop at a hot spring for a soak before dinner.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Altyn-Arashan and back
desc: Today we swap the car for a Russian army off-roader. The track into Altyn-Arashan fords rivers and climbs over rocky ground, and the ride itself is half the fun. It takes around two hours.

The valley sits among snowy peaks, pine forest and green meadows. You set the plan with your guide: an easy walk, a longer hike, a horse ride or a long soak in the natural hot springs. Lunch is in the valley.
Strong walkers can ask for an early start and a hike toward Ala-Kul Lake. This option has to be agreed before the tour.
In the afternoon we drive back down to Karakol. Dinner is our farewell meal, and a massage can be arranged if you want one.
itinerary.transfer: Karakol to Altyn-Arashan and back · 80 km · 5-6 h with off-road
itinerary.activity: Walking, hiking or riding · hot springs

itinerary.title: Karakol to Bishkek via Semenov Gorge and Cholpon-Ata
desc: In the morning your guide shows you Karakol. You visit the Dungan Mosque, built without a single nail, and the wooden Russian Orthodox church. Both tell the story of the many peoples who settled this town.
Then we drive into the Grigoriev and Semenov gorges. Pine forest, rivers and flower meadows fill these valleys, and there is time for a walk.
In Cholpon-Ata you take a boat out onto Issyk-Kul, with snowy ranges all around. It makes a good last look at the lake.
We return to Bishkek along the north shore and drop you at your hotel in the evening.
itinerary.activity: Town tour · gorge walk · boat ride

name: Song-Kul Yurts, Eagles & Karakol - 4 Days
accommodations: 2 nights at yurt, 1 night at hotel
summary: A private four-day trip that links Song-Kul and Issyk-Kul. You cross Kalmak-Ashuu Pass to a yurt camp on Song-Kul, ride a horse across its meadows and come down the 33 Parrots road. Then an eagle show, a second yurt night by Issyk-Kul, the red rocks of Jeti-Oguz and hot springs. Good for travellers short on time who still want both lakes.
highlights: Yurt nights at both Song-Kul and Issyk-Kul
Horse ride across the Song-Kul meadows
Felt workshop and home-cooked lunch in Kochkor
Boat ride and a swim on Issyk-Kul

blurb.hook: Two lakes, two yurt nights and one horse ride in four days.
blurb.text: Song-Kul over Kalmak-Ashuu Pass, then eagles in Bokonbayevo, Jeti-Oguz, hot springs and a swim from a boat on Issyk-Kul. Private, May to September.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Song-Kul via Kochkor and Kalmak-Ashuu
desc: We pick you up in Bishkek and head for the mountains. First stop is Burana Tower on the old Silk Road. You climb it for the view, then look around the ruins and the small museum.

The road runs through Boom Gorge to the Orto-Tokoy Reservoir, bright blue water against dry hills. In Kochkor a local family cooks lunch for you. Afterwards you visit a felt workshop where women make carpets by hand, the way it has been done for centuries.
In the afternoon we climb Kalmak-Ashuu Pass. Here the land turns to green pasture with grazing herds and wildflowers. After a photo stop at the top we drop down to Song-Kul.
You reach the yurt camp late in the afternoon. There is time for a walk along the shore before dinner. At night the sky over the lake is one of the clearest in the country.

itinerary.title: Song-Kul to Bokonbayevo via the 33 Parrots road
desc: Mornings at Song-Kul are fresh and quiet. After breakfast you ride a horse across the open meadows, with the lake in view the whole way. It is an easy ride and a real taste of nomad life.
Late in the morning we start down the 33 Parrots road, a chain of hairpin bends with big mountain views. At the bottom a short, easy walk leads to a waterfall. Lunch is in Kochkor.
In the afternoon we reach Bokonbayevo for the eagle show. A hunter works with his golden eagle in front of you and explains the tradition. You can hold the bird for a photo.
The night is at Bel-Tam yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore. Dinner is by the lake, and the evening ends around a bonfire.
itinerary.activity: Horse riding · 1-2 h · waterfall walk · eagle show

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Karakol via Skazka, Barskoon and Jeti-Oguz
desc: We follow the south shore east. In Skazka Canyon, the Fairytale Canyon, wind has shaped red sandstone into castles, animals and tall walls. Viewpoints above the canyon make good photo stops.
In Barskoon Gorge a short, easy path through pine forest leads to one of the finest waterfalls in the area. The air is cool and the water loud.
Jeti-Oguz is next, with its red cliffs called the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart. Your guide shares the legends behind them.
Late in the day you soak in natural hot springs with mountains all around. Then we drive on to Karakol, and the evening is yours.
itinerary.activity: Canyon walk · waterfall walk · hot springs

itinerary.title: Karakol to Bishkek via Grigoriev Gorge and Cholpon-Ata
desc: We start with a short look at Karakol. The wooden Dungan Mosque was built without nails in a Chinese style, and the Holy Trinity Cathedral shows the Russian side of the town's past. Your guide explains how these faiths have lived side by side. We also walk through the local bazaar.
Then we drive into the Grigoriev and Semenov gorges for a gentle walk among forest and rivers. A horse ride is possible here at extra cost.

In Cholpon-Ata you visit the Rukh Ordo open-air centre and the petroglyphs, stone carvings more than 2,000 years old. From May to September a boat takes you out on Issyk-Kul, and you can swim straight from the deck.
We reach Bishkek in the evening and drop you at your hotel.
itinerary.activity: Town tour · gorge walk · boat ride

name: Issyk-Kul Loop via Chong-Kemin - 5 Days
accommodations: 1 night at guesthouse, 1 night at hotel, 2 nights at yurt
activities: horse riding - 2 days, hiking - 1 day, sightseeing - 5 days
summary: Five days around the whole of Issyk-Kul, with more riding and cooking than a usual lake tour. You ride three hours into the Chong-Kemin mountains, bake boorsok with a local family, ride again into Kok-Jaiyk Valley to a yurt and finish with an eagle show and archery near Bokonbayevo. Suits travellers who want culture and time outdoors in one trip.
highlights: Three-hour horse ride in Chong-Kemin National Park
Boorsok cooking class with a local family
Ride into Kok-Jaiyk Valley and sleep in a yurt
Eagle show and archery class near Bokonbayevo

blurb.hook: Ride, cook and camp your way around Issyk-Kul.
blurb.text: Horses in Chong-Kemin and Kok-Jaiyk, boorsok with a local family, a boat on the lake, hot springs, Ak-Sai Canyon and a yurt by the water.

itinerary.title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin via Burana Tower
desc: We meet you at your hotel in Bishkek and drive to Burana Tower near Tokmok. You walk among old mausoleums and finds dug up by archaeologists, then climb the tower for a view over the Chuy Valley and the Tien Shan. A small museum and an open-air yard of gravestones and rock drawings fill in the history.
On the road we stop for samsa, baked in a clay tandoor at a local street stall. In Boom Gorge you try tea with milk and kattama, a layered onion flatbread.
In Chong-Kemin National Park you swap the car for a horse. The ride lasts three hours and climbs into the mountains, with the Tien Shan in view.
Back at the guesthouse, a local family shows you how to make boorsok, a Kyrgyz puffed pastry. You eat what you made at dinner and spend the night in the park.

itinerary.title: Chong-Kemin to Karakol via Cholpon-Ata
desc: After breakfast in the park we drive to Cholpon-Ata. You see the open-air petroglyph field and the Rukh Ordo cultural centre, a good primer on Kyrgyz history and culture.
Lunch is Kyrgyz food at a good restaurant in town. Then a boat takes you out on Issyk-Kul. From May to September you can swim from the boat, and life jackets are on board.
Next come the Grigoriev and Semenov gorges, two of the best-known valleys on the lake. Your guide tells you about the area as you go.
Around sunset we reach Karakol and head to natural hot springs by a mountain river. Dinner is at a local restaurant, and the night in a hotel.
itinerary.activity: Boat ride · gorge visit · hot springs

itinerary.title: Karakol to Kok-Jaiyk Valley via Jeti-Oguz
desc: Breakfast at the hotel, then a look around Karakol. We visit the Dungan Mosque and the Russian Orthodox church, two sides of the town's mixed history.
We drive out to Jeti-Oguz to see the red rock called the Seven Bulls. Here you get back in the saddle and ride deeper into Kok-Jaiyk Valley, between high peaks and glacier rivers.
The ride takes two to three hours and ends at a yurt camp, where lunch and a rest are waiting.
Before sunset there is time to walk around and take photos. Dinner and the night are in the yurt.

itinerary.title: Jeti-Oguz to Bokonbayevo via Barskoon and Skazka Canyon
desc: We start early to see sunrise on the Seven Bulls. Then we drive to Barskoon Valley, known for its waterfalls. Nearby stands a giant head of Yuri Gagarin, a tribute to the cosmonaut's training at Issyk-Kul.
A hike of one to two hours takes you to the main Barskoon waterfall.
Further along the south shore we stop at Skazka Canyon, the Fairytale Canyon, known for rocks in odd shapes. A 30-minute climb to a small hilltop gives you a view over the lake.
The night is at a yurt camp on the Issyk-Kul shore. It has showers, toilets, laundry and a bar with a lake view. There is free time before dinner, and you fall asleep to the sound of the waves.

itinerary.title: Bokonbayevo to Bishkek via Ak-Sai Canyon
desc: Breakfast, then free time until late morning for a swim or a slow start by the water.

Next is the eagle show, with three demonstrations. The hunter calls his eagle from far off to his hand, then stages a hunt with a fox fur. The last one is a real hunt on a live rabbit. After the show you get an archery lesson.

We then drive into the Ak-Sai canyons and the Canyon of Forgotten Rivers. At its entrance you can still see the beds of rivers that dried up long ago. Down by the lake a wild beach waits for a picnic lunch.
From there it is about 200 km back to Bishkek, where we drop you at your hotel.

name: Ak-Suu Three-Pass Trek to Ala-Kul - 5 Days
accommodations: 3 nights at yurt camp, 1 night at tent camp
summary: The best five days of the Ak-Suu Traverse, from Jergez Gorge back to Karakol. You cross Ailanysh Pass at 3,676 m, Ortok Pass at 3,650 m and Ala-Kul North Pass at 3,906 m, soak in the Altyn-Arashan hot springs and camp on the shore of Ala-Kul. Three nights are in yurts. For fit hikers who want the heart of the route in under a week.
highlights: Ailanysh Pass at 3,676 m above two quiet alpine lakes
Hot springs at Altyn-Arashan after three days on foot
Ala-Kul North Pass at 3,906 m, the top of the trek
A tent night on the shore of Ala-Kul at 3,550 m

blurb.hook: Three high passes, one turquoise lake, five days on foot.
blurb.text: The core of the Ak-Suu Traverse: Jergez Gorge, Ailanysh and Ortok passes, hot springs at Altyn-Arashan and a night by Ala-Kul. Yurts most nights.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Jergez Gorge on foot
desc: We meet in Karakol for a briefing and a gear check. A 30-minute drive takes us to Kara-Kyz village, and the walking starts right there.
Today has no pass. It is a warm-up day that lets your legs and lungs get used to the height.

The trail climbs gently up Jergez Gorge beside the river. Shepherd yurts dot the slopes, and families graze their horses in the upper valley. We sleep in a yurt at the head of the gorge, with the first real mountain views.

itinerary.title: Jergez Gorge to Almaluu Gorge over Ailanysh Pass
desc: This is where the traverse gets serious. We cross a small river and climb toward Ailanysh Pass at 3,676 m.
Just below the pass, two Ailanysh lakes lie at 3,445 m in a bowl of grey rock. They are cold, clear and very still. From the top you look out at the Ak-Suu glacier wall and peaks close to 4,000 m.
A long descent takes us into Almaluu Gorge. Shepherd families camp along this stretch, and stopping for tea with them is often the moment people remember most.
If you still have energy, there is an optional afternoon hike to a waterfall. The night is in a yurt camp at 2,800 m.

itinerary.title: Almaluu Gorge to Altyn-Arashan over Ortok Pass
desc: The morning is a steady 800 m climb up Almaluu Gorge to Ortok Pass at 3,650 m.
On the far side the land changes fast. Rock gives way to grass, grass gives way to pine forest, and the air warms as you drop.
Altyn-Arashan means Golden Spa in Kyrgyz, after its natural mineral springs. After three days on the trail, a late afternoon soak is exactly what your legs want.
We sleep in a yurt among the pines at 2,500 m. Rest well, because tomorrow is the biggest day.

itinerary.title: Altyn-Arashan to Ala-Kul Lake over Ala-Kul North Pass
desc: Today you climb 1,400 m, from the valley floor at 2,500 m to Ala-Kul North Pass at 3,906 m. The trail crosses alpine meadow, then boulder fields, then loose scree on the last steep stretch. Your guide sets the pace and the rest stops.
From the pass the whole Terskey Ala-Too range opens up. It is the widest and highest view of the trek.
A short descent brings you to Ala-Kul at 3,550 m. The glacier-fed water is a deep turquoise, ringed by peaks higher than five thousand metres.
We pitch the tents right by the water. Nights up here are cold, so bring warm layers.

itinerary.title: Ala-Kul Lake to Karakol through Karakol Gorge
desc: If the sky is clear, get up early. The peaks catch the sun before the lake does, and that first light gives the best photos of the trip.
After breakfast the trail heads west from the lake and down the upper Karakol Gorge. Pine forest and the river come back, and the walking is mostly downhill and kind to tired legs.
Halfway down, an old Soviet alpine base camp makes a natural tea stop. At the road a 4x4 waits to take you into Karakol.

name: Full Ak-Suu Traverse from Jyrgalan - 9 Days
accommodations: 3 nights at yurt camp, 2 nights at guesthouse, 3 nights at tent camp
summary: The whole Ak-Suu Traverse in nine days, from Jyrgalan village to the red cliffs of Jeti-Oguz. You camp by the Boz-Uchuk lakes, cross Ailanysh and Ortok passes, take a rest day in the Altyn-Arashan hot springs, then climb to Ala-Kul Pass at 3,906 m and walk out through Telety Valley. Made for fit trekkers with multi-day experience.
highlights: Tent night beside the Boz-Uchuk lakes at 3,400 m
A hidden waterfall in the upper Jergez Gorge
A full rest day in the Altyn-Arashan hot springs
Finish among the red Seven Bulls cliffs of Jeti-Oguz

blurb.hook: Nine days across the Terskey Ala-Too, end to end.
blurb.text: Jyrgalan to Jeti-Oguz on foot: the Boz-Uchuk lakes, Ailanysh Pass, a rest day in the Altyn-Arashan springs, Ala-Kul and Telety Valley. For seasoned trekkers.

itinerary.title: Karakol to Terim-Tor via Jyrgalan
desc: We drive about an hour east along Issyk-Kul to Jyrgalan. It was once a mining village and is now one of the country's best-known ecotourism spots.
After a briefing and a gear check, you set off on foot across high pastures and open ridges toward the Terim-Tor camp.
It is a steady first day, long enough to learn the ground and easy enough to warm up. Dinner and the night are in a yurt.

itinerary.title: Terim-Tor to the Boz-Uchuk Lakes over two passes
desc: Two passes in one day make this one of the hardest stages. Straight after breakfast you climb Terim-Tor Bulak Pass, gaining 480 m in just 1.4 km. It is steep but short.
From the valley floor the second climb, to Boz-Uchuk Pass at 3,363 m, is gentle, with only about 200 m of gain. Then the Boz-Uchuk lakes come into view below.
These glacial pools sit at 3,400 m and shift from deep green to turquoise as the sky changes. We camp beside the upper lake, where dusk is very still.

itinerary.title: Boz-Uchuk Lakes to Jergez Gorge and the waterfall
desc: A short climb over a ridge and down into the valley starts the day. Then the trail rises again to a pass at 3,524 m with a view of Tashtanbek Tor Bashi peak.
The main stage is short, so the afternoon is free. From camp we walk to a waterfall tucked into the upper gorge. Few people expect it, and it is well worth the walk.
The night is in a yurt camp in Jergez Gorge.
itinerary.activity: Trekking · 7 km + 5 km waterfall hike · +500 m / -700 m

itinerary.title: Jergez Gorge to Almaluu Valley over Ailanysh Pass
desc: From camp we climb to the first Ailanysh lake at 3,445 m and stop for a short break. The trail then steepens up to Ailanysh Pass at 3,676 m.
The two lakes under the pass are some of the quietest places on the route. Few people outside the traverse ever see them.
On the way down you face a 3,855 m peak and the icy Ak-Suu Wall. The trail drops steadily to the Almaluu valley and a camp by the river. After Day 2, this is the hardest day of the trek.

itinerary.title: Almaluu Valley to Altyn-Arashan over Ortok Pass
desc: By traverse standards this is an easier day. It opens with a short, steep climb of 800 m to Ortok Pass at 3,650 m.
The long way down changes everything around you. Rock turns to grass, grass to pine forest, and it gets warmer with every kilometre.
You follow the river into Altyn-Arashan in the afternoon. Tonight means a guesthouse, a hot shower and a real bed.

itinerary.title: Rest day in Altyn-Arashan
desc: No trail today. You rest in the valley and soak in the natural hot springs, outdoor mineral pools among the pines.
After five days of camps and passes, sleeping in and eating well is the whole plan. If you cannot sit still, a short morning walk up the valley is an option.
Make the most of it. Tomorrow brings the biggest climb of the traverse.

itinerary.title: Altyn-Arashan to Ala-Kul Lake over Ala-Kul Pass
desc: This is the toughest climbing day of all nine. You walk about 8 km up from 2,500 m to Ala-Kul Pass at 3,906 m, a gain of 1,400 m. The last 200 m are steep and rocky.
From the top the Terskey Ala-Too range opens in every direction. It is one of the widest views on the route.
A short descent leads to Ala-Kul at 3,550 m, turquoise and glacier-fed under peaks over 4,000 m. We camp by the lake.

itinerary.title: Ala-Kul Lake to Telety Valley
desc: Get up early if the sky is clear. The peaks light up before the water does, and it is the best photo of the whole trek.
After breakfast we walk north from the lake into Telety Valley. It is a gentler day, and the lower height helps the body recover.
There are plenty of places to camp. Our pick is a long flat spot about halfway up, where the river widens, with views of Telety to the southwest and back to the Ala-Kul passes.

itinerary.title: Telety Valley to Karakol via Jeti-Oguz
desc: The last morning on the trail. Over Telety Pass it is under two easy hours down to the river valley on the far side.
Then the path drops toward Jeti-Oguz, and the red sandstone cliffs of the Seven Bulls appear. After nine days of grey granite and ice, the colour is a fine way to finish.
A short drive takes you from Jeti-Oguz back to Karakol.

name: Karakol Peak Base & Ala-Kul Trek - 4 Days
accommodations: 1 night at yurt camp, 2 nights at tent camp
summary: A slower Ala-Kul trek with one extra day in the mountains. You walk up Karakol Gorge, reach the foot of Karakol Peak (5,216 m) among moraines and hanging glaciers, camp by Ala-Kul, then cross Ala-Kul Pass at 3,906 m down to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs. Two nights at altitude before the lake make the big climb easier. For hikers who would rather not rush.
highlights: Hike to the base of 5,216 m Karakol Peak
Two nights in tents, far from roads and towns
Sunrise over Ala-Kul at 3,550 m
Ala-Kul Pass at 3,906 m, then hot springs below

blurb.hook: Ala-Kul with an extra day under Karakol Peak.
blurb.text: Karakol Gorge, the glaciers at the foot of Karakol Peak, a night by Ala-Kul and the pass down to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs. Better acclimatised, less rushed.

itinerary.title: Karakol to the lower camp in Karakol Gorge
desc: We meet in Karakol for a briefing and a gear check, then drive south into the national park.
The trail starts in pine forest along the Karakol River. It climbs steadily through the shady gorge and out into alpine meadow. Karakol Peak shows itself for the first time, still far off.
After 5 to 6 hours on foot we reach the lower yurt camp at about 2,500 m. Dinner is hot and plentiful. We keep the pace easy today, because tomorrow the ground gets harder.
itinerary.transfer: Karakol to Karakol Gorge · private vehicle

itinerary.title: Lower camp to high camp via the Karakol Peak approach
desc: This is the day that sets this trek apart. After breakfast we leave the main valley and climb toward the Karakol Peak massif.
We do not go for the summit. The route takes you to the foot of the peak at around 3,400 to 3,600 m, among moraines and hanging glaciers. Your guide explains the terrain and the history of the peak.
Late in the afternoon we drop to the high camp. Expect a cold night, a clear sky and real silence.

itinerary.title: High camp to Ala-Kul Lake
desc: Two nights at height have done their work. The 1,100 m climb to Ala-Kul at 3,550 m still takes effort, but it feels easier with good acclimatisation.
The trail crosses boulder fields and passes a high mountain hut before the lake opens up in full. The water is deep turquoise and fed by glaciers, with peaks over 4,000 m around it.
Lunch is at the shore, and the afternoon is yours by the lake. Dinner and the night are at the tent camp.

itinerary.title: Ala-Kul Lake to Karakol via Ala-Kul Pass and Altyn-Arashan
desc: After one more early morning at the lake, we climb 350 m to Ala-Kul Pass at 3,906 m. The top gives the widest view of the trek, with the Terskey Ala-Too in every direction.
The way down starts on loose scree, so we take it slowly. Lower down the valley turns green and Altyn-Arashan comes into view.
Lunch is at a guesthouse, then you soak in the hot springs, outdoor pools among the pines. A private vehicle brings you back to Karakol in the afternoon.
